_: EP 18 — CQRS. The STATION STRIP register (references/station-strip.md), wearing EP 16's palette and design system unchanged: `stripe-mesh`, white canvas, deep-navy ink #0D253D, ONE saturated hue (indigo #533AFD) that is a CTA and an accent and nothing else. What is NEW is the FIELD — the director supplied a stripe gradient (32deg, #FFFFFF → #78B8F9 → #5667FF → #4D2FF9) under fractalNoise grain at 0.210, overlay-blended, tiled at 120px. That is the `RibbonField` MACHINE this kit already ships with a different stop list, so the machine is kept exactly and the stops are taken verbatim from the supplied CSS; grain amount 42 reproduces the 0.210 opacity exactly ((42/100)*0.5). The supplied stops are azure/indigo and sit a few degrees from the brand's own #533AFD, so the field and the accent are one system rather than two. TERMINOLOGY AND ATTRIBUTION ARE SOURCED: CQRS was named by Greg Young in 2010 and is a separation of the MODEL, derived from Bertrand Meyer's Command-Query Separation in Object-Oriented Software Construction (1988), which separates METHODS; Young's own repeated correction is that CQRS is neither event sourcing nor eventual consistency nor a top-level architecture, and that most systems should not use it. THE FIGURES ARE ONE WORKED SYSTEM'S, NOT INDUSTRY FACTS, and the film frames them that way on screen — a single order-history screen: six tables in the join, p99 840 ms on the normalised read against 4 ms on the projected row; a projector consuming OrderPlaced/OrderPaid/OrderShipped/OrderCancelled; replica lag measured at 340 ms p50 and 1.4 s p99; a read model rebuilt by replaying 4,200,000 events. Nothing on screen is presented as a universal number.
title: Write Here.
subtitle: CQRS splits one model in two, so each half only has to be good at one thing.
hook: One table served both jobs. It was bad at both.
next: Next: event sourcing, and the log you are not allowed to edit
_theme: EP 16's palette exactly — the construction and the palette are the series, and this episode's own signature is the FIELD, not a new colour. Indigo stays the single filled hue; #78B8F9 and #4D2FF9 arrived with the supplied gradient and live ONLY inside it, never as a flat fill, exactly the way ruby and magenta are handled in stripe-mesh.
_voice: Unchanged from EP 13–17 — same voice id, same model, same settings. Every line opens on an instruction verb.
_music: Same 84bpm grid as EP 13–17 so scene lengths snap identically across the run.
_vo: Nine lines. Definition then consequence, one clause a sentence. Act one is the mechanism and every line is an instruction to build something; act two opens by making the viewer pay for it, and the last line refuses the pattern by default — which is Greg Young's own position and the honest end to a CQRS episode.

vo.text: Count the joins behind one screen. Six tables, one query, and it runs on every single page load.
Split the model in two. Commands change state. Queries answer questions. The two never share a table.
Send an intent, not a row. A command is accepted or rejected, and it hands back almost nothing.
Shape the read side like the screen. One row, no joins… already answered before anybody asked.
Watch the projector do the work. It reads each event once, then upserts the row the screen needs.
Now pay for it. The write landed, the read has not… and your user just hit refresh.
Close that gap deliberately. Return the new state, or pin one user to the write side for a moment.
Treat the read model as disposable. Drop it, replay the log… and build it back from nothing.
Then refuse it by default. This is NOT event sourcing, and one model is usually the right answer.

_shots: No Kling. The station-strip register carries a full episode on graphics alone; the supplied stripe field is the depth.
